text:
Last night's Integration Debt Night at Kestrelmoor's Flatiron office drew about 60 people, and the room's biggest takeaway was clear: AI agents don't stall on the model, they stall on the plumbing.

Marcus Feldane, founder of Quillary, put it plainly: agent pilots fail at the integration seam. His team's rule is to wire up data access before choosing a model. When he asked the room, about 40 of 60 hands went up for having an agent pilot stall on data access.

Priya Raman-Holt, VP Platform at Tallowbrook, shared how her team keeps 140 partner integrations running with just three engineers: "We stopped building connectors one by one and started publishing a spec. Partners build to it now."

The best moment was where they disagreed. Priya thinks partners should own their connectors. Marcus thinks the platform has to own them or quality drifts. I left without a clear winner, and I suspect the answer depends on how much you can afford to let quality vary.

My takeaway: before the next agent pilot, ask who owns the integrations and whether a spec exists, then pick the model.

Thanks to the Kestrelmoor team for hosting.

What has your experience been: who should own the connector?
